## Natural history notes

A small, dark skipper butterfly characterized by mottled brown wings, pale spotting, and a low, quick flight close to the ground. In Florida, it is found in dry open woodlands, scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, forest edges, and other sunny habitats where oaks are present. Adults visit flowers for nectar and often perch on bare ground, leaves, or low vegetation, while the caterpillars feed on oak leaves and shelter in folded or tied leaves.
